purpose: Extend gitleaks secret-scanning evidence beyond the one synthetic github-pat fixture (directory-mode only) to (a) this repository's actual commit history via `gitleaks git` and (b) a fresh `gitleaks dir` pass over the live worktree, per the critic's correction that gap 0 (credentials off the live checkout) needs a working-tree scan and gap 1 needs git-history coverage. Guarded gitleaks on PATH only; the unskipped full-history scan is explicitly avoided per AGENTS.md (it exhausted host memory earlier).
preregistered: Expected: `gitleaks git . --config .gitleaks.toml --max-target-megabytes 2 --redact --no-banner --report-format json` over this worktree's reachable commit history, and `gitleaks dir .` over the current working tree, each bounded to 2MB per target file via --max-target-megabytes and run once under the guarded wrapper's memory/time caps (4G/6G, 600s). A clean result on both would extend gap 1's git-history coverage without closing gap 2 (scanning is not proof of no secret anywhere) or gap 0 (which is a login-policy claim, not a fully scannable artifact). Any finding would be recorded verbatim with its rule id and location, not re-run to seek a different outcome; any file skipped for size would be recorded as incomplete coverage per AGENTS.md.
